data.title: Does COG Financial Services (ASX:COG) Deserve A Spot On Your Watchlist?
data.description:
Investors are often guided by the idea of discovering 'the next big thing', even if that means buying 'story stocks' without any revenue, let alone profit. But the reality is that when a company loses money each year, for long enough, its investors will usually take their share of those losses. A loss-making company is yet to prove itself with profit, and eventually the inflow of external capital may dry up.

If this kind of company isn't your style, you like companies that generate revenue, and even earn profits, then you may well be interested in COG Financial Services (ASX:COG). Even if this company is fairly valued by the market, investors would agree that generating consistent profits will continue to provide COG Financial Services with the means to add long-term value to shareholders.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

COG Financial Services' Earnings Per Share Are Growing

If you believe that markets are even vaguely efficient, then over the long term you'd expect a company's share price to follow its earnings per share (EPS) outcomes. That makes EPS growth an attractive quality for any company. To the delight of shareholders, COG Financial Services has achieved impressive annual EPS growth of 39%, compound, over the last three years. Growth that fast may well be fleeting, but it should be more than enough to pique the interest of the wary stock pickers.

It's often helpful to take a look at earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margins, as well as revenue growth, to get another take on the quality of the company's growth. While we note COG Financial Services achieved similar EBIT margins to last year, revenue grew by a solid 9.7% to AU$403m. That's a real positive.

In the chart below, you can see how the company has grown earnings and revenue, over time. For finer detail, click on the image.

View our latest analysis for COG Financial Services

You don't drive with your eyes on the rear-view mirror, so you might be more interested in this free report showing analyst forecasts for COG Financial Services' future profits.

Are COG Financial Services Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

It's pleasing to see company leaders with putting their money on the line, so to speak, because it increases alignment of incentives between the people running the business, and its true owners. Shareholders will be pleased by the fact that insiders own COG Financial Services shares worth a considerable sum. Indeed, they hold AU$38m worth of its stock. This considerable investment should help drive long-term value in the business. Those holdings account for over 11% of the company; visible skin in the game.

Does COG Financial Services Deserve A Spot On Your Watchlist?

COG Financial Services' earnings per share have been soaring, with growth rates sky high. This level of EPS growth does wonders for attracting investment, and the large insider investment in the company is just the cherry on top. At times fast EPS growth is a sign the business has reached an inflection point, so there's a potential opportunity to be had here. So at the surface level, COG Financial Services is worth putting on your watchlist; after all, shareholders do well when the market underestimates fast growing companies. It is worth noting though that we have found 3 warning signs for COG Financial Services that you need to take into consideration.

There's always the possibility of doing well buying stocks that are not growing earnings and do not have insiders buying shares. But for those who consider these important metrics, we encourage you to check out companies that do have those features. data.title: Earnings Miss Might Change The Case For Ziff Davis Stock
data.description:
• Ziff Davis reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$289.33 million, compared with US$306.53 million a year earlier, alongside a net loss of US$28.69 million from continuing operations and basic and diluted loss per share of US$0.85.
  • Across the first nine months of 2026, Ziff Davis generated US$843.71 million in sales and US$618.03 million in net income, with very high basic and diluted earnings per share of US$17.22 that contrast sharply with the loss per share from continuing operations.
  • We will look at how Ziff Davis's investment narrative holds up in light of weaker quarterly sales and a larger loss from continuing operations.

Compare Ziff Davis with a curated group of peers that currently screen well on fundamentals using our hand picked 21 high quality undiscovered gems as a starting list for your next idea.

Ziff Davis Investment Narrative Recap

To stay invested in Ziff Davis, you need to believe the mix shift toward subscription, cybersecurity and martech can offset pressure on ad driven properties over time. The latest quarter adds tension to that view. Sales from continuing operations softened and the loss from those activities widened, which keeps the core profitability question very much open.

The key near term catalyst is how management deploys the sizeable cash and balance sheet capacity after the Connectivity sale, including acquisitions and buybacks. The biggest risk is that search driven and healthcare related media assets stay under pressure, so incremental capital fails to lift revenue or margins meaningfully against those headwinds.

RetailMeNot’s 20th National Cash Back Day event is a useful real time test of Ziff Davis’s Shopping and affiliate ecosystem. The promotion spans more than 3,500 retailers and offers elevated cash back rates, so it gives a live read on consumer engagement, advertiser appetite and how well the RetailMeNot platform converts traffic into monetizable transactions.

If these types of events keep users active and brands spending through the holidays, they can support the push toward more performance oriented digital advertising and e commerce that analysts have focused on as a catalyst. If uptake is weaker than hoped, it would underline the risk that Tech & Shopping properties remain under structural pressure from search changes and tougher competition.

Ziff Davis' current earnings are a loss of US$29.7 million, while analysts expect earnings to reach US$34.8 million by 2029. This implies an earnings swing of about US$64.5 million, alongside a projected annual revenue decline rate of 7.2% and forecast revenues of US$1.2 billion in 2029.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternative view focuses less on buybacks and more on the risk that Ziff Davis cannot fully offset weaker ad driven income. The most cautious analysts already assumed revenue of about US$1.2b and earnings near US$52.2 million by 2029 before this earnings miss, so their story now looks much tougher than the consensus path. These forecasts were all set before the latest quarter, so you should expect opinions, and possibly the numbers behind them, to move around as new data comes through.
